## Ruling on deliverable 1 — **(B) is not mechanically readable, and I have six measurements from one shift that say why**

`domain:devx` execution PM seat (#6023), session `session_012GKcPZbMoGq7WPzKLfRBTU`. This card's first deliverable is *"the decision, NOT a gate"*, and it lands in this lane. Taking it.

### ⭐ The evidence is the inverse of the class, and that is what settles it

Class (B) is: **a claim in prose that no instrument can read**, so it goes stale unnoticed. In a single shift on this seat, the *mirror* failure fired **six** times: prose that an instrument **did** read — as an instance of the very thing it was describing.

| # | the reader | what it read as an instance | cost |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1 | `check-clause2-carriers`' `CLAUSE2_KEY_LINE` | my standing-rules bullet **explaining** the two legal spellings | the card declared `yes`; `needs:contract-review` hung on a `scripts/`-only diff (#17098) |
| 2 | a dev's new spelling pin | the script's own comment **quoting** the broken template to explain it | pin read 3 violations on a clean tree; fixed by anchoring on the assignment form |
| 3 | the same pin's first regex (backtracking `X{3,}` + `[^"]+`) | a **correct** template | a correct line read as broken — caught only by a firing control against `origin/main` |
| 4 | my pre-landing control | `:569`, a comment **mentioning** `mktemp` | predicted 3, read 4 |
| 5 | my landing probe's negative leg | the fix's **own new comments** quoting the broken shape | said `2 → 0`; reads **3** on the landed tree. Trusting it would have read a successful landing as a failure |
| 6 | my own defect-population count | `bump-objectui.sh`'s comments **explaining why `mapfile` is avoided** (`:349`–`:365`) | nearly manufactured a two-instance population that would have justified building a whole gate (ruled in #17141) |

⇒ **Every mechanical reader of prose I exercised in one shift confused MENTION for USE.** Three were instruments in the repo; three were probes I wrote myself; one nearly caused a gate to be built on a fabricated population.

**That is the ruling's whole basis.** A class-(B) gate must read a claim written in prose and decide whether it is still true. Before it can do that it must decide whether the sentence is *asserting* the fact or *quoting* it — and that is the same use/mention judgement that failed six times, in a repo whose text is unusually dense with prose that quotes patterns in order to explain them. ⛔ Building a (B) reader means building the thing that is already the measured failure mode, and pointing it at the hardest possible input.

⇒ **Answer to (1): no gate. And "no gate" here is not a shrug — it is a finding with a mechanism.**

### On the candidates the card names, briefly

- **Semantic diffing of prose against source** — needs use/mention resolution as a *precondition*. ⛔ Rejected on the evidence above.
- **A required "this restates X" annotation on restating passages** — ⚠️ this is the interesting one and I am ⛔ **not** ruling it out, because it *converts (B) into (A)*: an annotation is an identifier, and #13556's ruling already says a corpus joins the shared resolver by registration. But it prices in an authoring burden on every restating passage repo-wide, and this card explicitly has **no population count**. ⇒ ⛔ Cannot be sized, let alone justified, until someone counts. Recorded as the only live route, deliberately unpursued.
- **Nothing** — taken, with the discipline below.

### Deliverable 2: the discipline, plus a second line the six measurements earn

The card's measured discipline is right and I adopt it verbatim in substance: **when repairing a claim, sweep for the claim's own FIGURES and TOKENS, not for the identifier or the sentence shape.**

⭐ Today's evidence earns a **counterpart** for whoever writes the instrument rather than the repair: **anchor a text-reading pattern on the assignment or definition form, and run it against a known tree as a firing control before trusting its number.** In four of the six cases that single step was what caught the error; in the two where it was skipped (my #4 and #5), the wrong number was published. `^[A-Z_]+="\$\(mktemp` settled #5 in one command after `grep -c 'mktemp'` had misled twice.

⇒ The two lines are a pair: one for the repairer, one for the instrument author, and they fail in opposite directions.

### ⛔ What I am NOT claiming

- ⛔ **My six are not a census either.** One seat, one shift, and every one surfaced because I happened to be running probes — the same biased-sample caveat this card puts on its own four. ⚠️ I am contributing a **mechanism**, ⛔ not a rate, and the population count this card asks for remains unmeasured and still first-order for any remedy that costs anything.
- ⛔ I did not sweep `objectui`, as the card notes nobody has.
- ⛔ Not folding in (A) or (C), per the card's instruction. Confirming (A)'s premise only: `scripts/symbol-anchors.mjs` exists on `origin/main` `06d38fb928` with **16** `defineCorpus` occurrences, so the shared resolver and its registration mechanism are real and #17065 is tractable on its own terms.

### ⚠️ Blocker on landing — the ruling is mine, the landing is not

Deliverable 2 says the sentence goes *"where a repairer reads it."* Measured: **`AGENTS.md` carries 2 sweep/repair mentions; `CLAUDE.md` carries 0**, and I found no non-governed candidate home under `docs/`. ⇒ The natural site is **`AGENTS.md`, a governed surface** — which this seat ⛔ may never flip, arm or merge.

⇒ This card is now the same shape as #16949: **ruled, but not landable by this lane.** ⛔ I am not dispatching it, and I am not moving it to `pm:awaiting-maintainer` unilaterally — the ruling above may be all it needed, and whoever owns the governed-surface merge can take the two sentences from here.

⚠️ That is the **third** card this shift whose remedy is correct, small, and outside this seat's authority (#15233, #16949, this). Recorded because it is starting to look like the reason this lane's `pm:queue` reads larger than its dispatchable set — #16688's finding, arriving from a different direction.
